Theme

Money, work & business

export verb and noun

also exports, exporting, exportation, ship abroad, exporter

classical

Cic. Flacc. 67: aurum … ex Ītaliā … Hierosolymam exportārī
Cic. Verr. 2.2.176: magnum numerum frūmentī … Syrācūsīs (Lewis & Short)

exportō, exportāre, exportāvī, exportātum

verb, first conjugation

carry out; export

To carry out, and so to send goods out of a country (Lewis & Short); it is also simply to carry something out of a house or a town.

Other words

  • ēvehō, ēvehere, ēvexī, ēvectum — carry out, ship out

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Varr. RR 1.16.6: mercēs, opposed to invehere (Lewis & Short)

    To carry out by cart or ship; Varro sets ēvehere and invehere side by side for what a farm sends out and brings in. Its other senses are to raise up (Hor. C. 1.1.6) and, in the passive, to ride or sail out.

  • exportātiō, exportātiōnis f. — export, exporting (the noun)

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 2.13

    Cicero’s noun, once (Lewis & Short), beside invectiō, import. The goods themselves are mercēs: exports, mercēs quae exportantur.

Examples

  • Cum aurum Jūdaeōrum nōmine quotannīs ex Ītaliā et ex omnibus nostrīs prōvinciīs Hierosolymam exportārī solēret, Flaccus sānxit ēdictō nē ex Asiā exportārī licēret.

    Since gold was regularly exported every year in the name of the Jews from Italy and all our provinces to Jerusalem, Flaccus forbade its export from Asia by edict.Cic. Flacc. 67

  • Jam vērō et eārum rērum quibus abundārēmus, exportātiō, et eārum quibus egērēmus invectiō certē nūlla esset, nisi iīs mūneribus hominēs fungerentur.

    Again, there would certainly be no export of the things we have in plenty, and no import of those we lack, if people did not do this work.Cic. Off. 2.13

See also import, merchant, business, goods.
